title: On Arguing the point for an hour
subtitle: 社区社会 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）
meta: 主题语境：社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）　|　核心词汇：argue　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 argue 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the shopkeeper ① argued the point for an hour year after year, and every buyer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the shopkeeper ② argues the point for an hour for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ argue the point for an hour at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ argued the point for an hour before — a line in the account for July 1962 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Arguing the point for an hour year after year, the shopkeeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ argue for a wider road for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Argue for a wider road at once and never mention it again.

By 1975 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the account, and a new buyer from the next shop ⑧ argues for a wider road year after year every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the counter, said nothing at all; she simply  argued the point for an hour again when nobody else would.

To argue the point for an hour, my mother said in 1980, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody argues the point for an hour for the whole place again and somebody must argue the point for an hour year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 争论（一般过去式 argued the point for an hour：1968 年掌柜头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 争论（一般现在 argues the point for an hour：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 争论（不定式 to argue the point for an hour：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 争论（过去完成时 had argued the point for an hour：1962 年七月的账本上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 争论（动名词 arguing the point for an hour 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 据理主张（argue for a wider road：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去据理主张主张修一条更宽的路）
G. v. 据理主张（argue for a wider road：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 争论（后段两处：新来的买主照例 argues for a wider road，而母亲又一次 argued the point for an hour）

items.q: argued the point for an hour

answers.why: argue 意为“争论”，1968 年掌柜年年地争论为这一点争了一个钟头，那是铺子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 argued。
argue 意为“争论”，自那以后掌柜替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 argues。
argue 意为“争论”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯争论为这一点争了一个钟头”，此处为不定式 to argue the point for an hour。
argue 意为“争论”，账本里 七月 那行字说明早在 1975 年之前就有人争论过，故用过去完成时 had argued。
argue 意为“争论”，掌柜说“争论为这一点争了一个钟头这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 arguing the point for an hour 作主语。
argue 意为“据理主张”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去据理主张主张修一条更宽的路”，should ever 之后用原形 argue for a wider road。
argue 意为“据理主张”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻据理主张主张修一条更宽的路（argue for a wider road at once），以后再也不要提起。
argue 意为“争论”，新来的买主每个月份都照例据理主张主张修一条更宽的路，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 argues。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1968 年，掌柜年年地争论为这一点争了一个钟头；铺子里每一个买主都说这是头一回。（argued the point for an hour）
多年以后，掌柜仍替所有人做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（argues the point for an hour）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯争论为这一点争了一个钟头这件事本身。（to argue the point for an hour）
早在 1962 年就有人争论为这一点争了一个钟头，七月那天账本上的一行字就是证据。（had argued the point for an hour）
掌柜说过，年年地争论为这一点争了一个钟头这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（arguing the point for an hour 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻据理主张主张修一条更宽的路，以后再也不要提起。（argue for a wider road，祈使句）
answers: In 1968 the shopkeeper argued the point for an hour year after year, and every buyer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three months on, the shopkeeper still argues the point for an hour for the whole place without being asked.
My mother said later that to argue the point for an hour at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had argued the point for an hour long before 1975, and the line in the account for July proves it.
Arguing the point for an hour year after year, the shopkeeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Argue for a wider road at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 argue 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1968 the shopkeeper argued the point for an hour year after year, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the shopkeeper argues the point for an hour for the whole place whenever the shop asks.
Arguing the point for an hour year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever argue for a wider road for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new buyer from the next shop argues for a wider road year after year every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother argued the point for an hour again, and the shop remembered that half.
